newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HARDING LEAVES CHELSEA STAKE TO HIS OWN COMPANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HARDING LEAVES CHELSEA STAKE TO HIS OWN COMPANY.

text.p: Matthew Harding, the Chelsea vice-chairman killed in a helicopter crash last week, has left his multi-million-pound stake in the English premier league club to his own company, the News of the World newspaper reported on Sunday.

Harding, who bought Chelsea's Stamford Bridge ground for 16.5 million pounds sterling ($26.3 million) last year and also owned 36 million shares in the company worth 30 million pounds ($48 million), decreed in his will that the company should be administered by his Benfield Group, the paper said.
While Harding was the vice-chairman of the club he was also its major benefactor. Bates will continue to run the club with money left by Harding and administered by his chosen executors.

Harding built up a personal fortune of around 150 million pounds ($240 million) which made him Britain's 89th richest man, through the Benfield Group, a re-insurance company he joined as a tea-boy in the 1970s.
He was killed, along with four others, when their helicopter crashed returning from Chelsea's league cup match against Bolton on Tuesday.
He was remembered on an emotional day at Stamford Bridge on Saturday when Chelsea played Tottenham in a premier league match.
Before the match the players of both teams and a capacity crowd of 28,373 stood for a minute's silence.
Harding's widow Ruth and their four children were also at the match. His empty seat was covered in flowers and a Chelsea banner.

Chelsea won the match 3-1 and player-manager Ruud Gullit, who scored the opening goal, said afterwards: "The victory was dedicated to Matthew. But today wasn't about playing football for three points. It was about going out there and winning for him -- and he would have liked that."
His body is to be cremated next week and the ashes sprinkled on the pitch at Stamford Bridge.
